question: Should OpenClaw adopt persisted `SessionEntry` byte-compaction retry hysteresis with the current 1 MiB/10% material-growth threshold before landing this PR?
rationale: The code appears correct, but the branch changes core session-state policy by persisting retry metadata and suppressing future byte-triggered compactions for the same active transcript until a material-growth condition is met.

options.title: Accept Current Hysteresis
options.body: Land this PR with the additive retry metadata and current growth threshold because it directly stops every-turn byte compaction loops while preserving token-triggered compaction.

options.title: Tune Threshold First
options.body: Ask for a different material-growth threshold and matching regression updates before merging the persisted session-state behavior.

options.title: Pause For Broader Compaction Policy
options.body: Hold this PR if owners want the broader compaction-rate-limit and stale-usage discussions resolved before adding a narrower byte-trigger retry rule.

recommendation.title: Accept Current Hysteresis
recommendation.body: Land this PR with the additive retry metadata and current growth threshold because it directly stops every-turn byte compaction loops while preserving token-triggered compaction.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged fixes by this owner changed the same preflight compaction gate and make them the strongest routing candidate for the retry-policy decision.
